texts.text: A pile of unrecognizably mangled bodies that fell from one of the upper floors.
A scattered group of Le Kaki are busily scouring through the gore, pocketing what Golden Hide dregs and eyeballs they can get their hands on.

texts.speaker: Impatient Customer
texts.text: That way... Maybe there's more to gather over there...? Dammit, I took the wrong spot!

texts.speaker: Desperate Customer
texts.text: This spot is mine. Fuck off!

texts.speaker: Rodion
texts.text: Whoa, you're a prickly one, aren'tcha. Fine, fine~ we'll back off~

texts.speaker: Destitute Customer
texts.text: Hey! Lift your foot. Didn't you just step on an eyeball?!

texts.speaker: Ishmael
texts.text: ... Uh, are you talking to me?

texts.speaker: Destitute Customer
texts.text: Did I see that wrong...? Whatever. Stop skulking around, then! You're throwing me off!

texts.speaker: Ishmael
texts.text: ... Hey, don't you think you should apologize if you got the wrong idea? *sigh* Actually, never mind.
<color=#E1B643>.......</color>
A soft and warm peal of laughter brushes past the fingertips laid against the wall.
A pale light, reminiscent of the Golden Bough, glimmers beneath its surface.
A wall patched over with Golden Hide.
The presence is faint, but something about it feels like the Golden Bough.

texts.speaker: Treatment Customer
texts.text: Thank goodness I booked my dermal perm before the trend died! Once they layer the curl into every ridge of my skin, nobody will be able to tear their eyes away from me!

texts.speaker: Eye-shopping Customer
texts.text: Got any empty bottles left? A spare palm would do, too.

texts.speaker: Rodion
texts.text: I... don't think we have any empty bottles or... spare palms... Sorry... ha... ha...

texts.speaker: Eye-shopping Customer
texts.text: Damn. I don't have enough eyeballs for this season's new collection...
The customer gnaws anxiously at their fingernails.
"Coverage That Never Fades! Feel the Refreshing Lymph of Freshly Shed Skin! Instant Sellout!"
... Still seems unnecessary to inspect the product itself.

texts.speaker: Yi Sang
texts.text: Dante. I am well aware that circumstances weigh heavily upon us... But ought we not hasten to find Meursault?

texts.speaker: Faust
texts.text: No further explanation from my side is necessary.

texts.speaker: Ishmael
texts.text: Was there something else you needed to check? Let's make it quick and get moving. We need to find Meursault ASAP.

texts.speaker: Gregor
texts.text: *puff* Can't exactly take a proper break when I know one of us could be experiencing the worst thing out there. Let's go if you fellas are all rested up.

texts.speaker: Hong Lu
texts.text: Do you suppose Meursault is all right? Being cast out into a strange place like this, all on your own... It'd leave anyone terribly lost and afraid.

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <I... don't think he'd feel lost and afraid... But yeah, best we hurry up and find him.>

texts.speaker: Hong Lu
texts.text: Fuhu... Then let's be on our way!
Sinclair is still huffing, apparently not yet over his anger.

texts.speaker: Sinclair
texts.text: Um... Manager... Shouldn't we hurry and start looking for Meursault?

texts.speaker: Don Quixote
texts.text: Hath the time arrived for us to resume our adventure? Verily, I remain ever at the ready!

texts.speaker: Heathcliff
texts.text: Bloody hell...
Heathcliff is pacing back and forth restlessly.

texts.speaker: Heathcliff
texts.text: Oh. Are we movin' again, then?

texts.speaker: Outis
texts.text: Please rest more if you remain fatigued, Executive Manager. Give the order, and I, Outis, shall detach a search party and...

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <It's okay. I should go with you guys.>

texts.speaker: Outis
texts.text: As expected of our Executive Manager. You are an example to every unit under your command...
Outis showers me with praise. Didn't know public restrooms came with showers.

texts.speaker: Rodion
texts.text: We ready to go? Man, I sure hope we won't see another pile of corpses fallin' down on us. I don't wanna get crushed to death under a pile of rotting meat... That'd be the stuff of 3 nights-long-nightmare.

texts.speaker: Ryōshū
texts.text: G.G., C.H.
Gotta Go, Chore Hour? Or... Get Going, Clockhead...?
I'll go and ask Sinclair later.
*knock* *knock*

texts.speaker: Hong Lu
texts.text: Hello? Is anybody in~?

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <The door's locked... Is there nobody inside?>

texts.speaker: Ryōshū
texts.text: Clock. M.Y.H.

texts.speaker: Sinclair
texts.text: Clock, move your head, she says... Eep!
Ryōshū's scabbard rattles menacingly, swinging in Sinclair's direction.
It seems Araya has fallen into this peculiar space alongside us.

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <We should probably check somewhere else first.>

texts.speaker: Outis
texts.text: Hm... It's not even budging.

texts.speaker: Outis
texts.text: Did you not hear what I said? The door's not budging.

texts.speaker: Heathcliff
texts.text: *yawn*

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <Heathcliff... I think she's talking to you.>

texts.speaker: Heathcliff
texts.text: ... The door won't budge, yeah. What do you want me to do about it?

texts.speaker: Outis
texts.text: What an absurd question. An obstacle emerges—you and that bat of yours terminate it without any thought given to the risk involved or the tactics available. Isn't that supposed to be your day-to-day doctrine of action?

texts.speaker: Outis
texts.text: The location beyond is yet to be screened, Executive Manager. Please fall back to a defensible distance. Heathcliff shall breach the door and scout ahead.

texts.speaker: Heathcliff
texts.text: Bloody hell, you've got some nerve telling me to put that door in! One look round and you can tell they spent a fortune on this place... What if they make us foot the bill after I've smashed it to bits?

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <... It's fine. No harm in trying. Smash it.>

texts.speaker: Heathcliff
texts.text: Huh...?

texts.speaker: Heathcliff
texts.text: All right, you wanted it, Clock.
Heathcliff swung his bat with all his might, only to be thrown backward as if something had shoved him away.

texts.speaker: Outis
texts.text: Hmm. It seems it can't be broken by physical means, Executive Manager.
The restroom door is shut. If it can't even be broken down, there's no reason to bother with it.
... (She gazes at me without a word. The serene smile on her face suggests that she regards us favorably.)

parts.notes: Can you tell us where we are again?

texts.text: ... It's the restroom.

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <Right...>

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <Hang on... She can interpret my ticking?!>
... (She says nothing more, but her smile lingers still.>

parts.notes: What is your relationship with Demian?

texts.text: ... Keep following the star, then someday...

texts.speaker: Sinclair
texts.text: ... Star...
Sinclair seems to sink inward, lost in deep thought.

parts.notes: What kind of being are you?

texts.text: (She does not reply. It seems any attempt to uncover her identity will prove futile.)
A burning clock head comes into view. There's nothing different from the usual, but... why does it feel oddly unfamiliar?
Familiar golden light leaks through a narrow gap between the tiles.
I can almost hear the faint murmuring of conversation between people.
I peer through the gap, but the glare of the light is too bright for me to see anything.

texts.speaker: Treatment Customer
texts.text: Strangers—stop checking me out. I'm halfway through my makeover treatment. You couldn't tell who I was even if you tried.

texts.speaker: Treatment Customer
texts.text: *sigh* This is why I hate coming down here. I suppose it can't be helped—the first floor is the only place that provides the service...

texts.speaker: Treatment Customer
texts.text: Stop staring at me!

texts.speaker: Treatment Customer
texts.text: Stop staring at me!

markers.notes: Salon Heat Lamp (with Pwie, after entering Footwear Hall).

texts.speaker: Pwie
texts.text: What's this?

texts.speaker: Hong Lu
texts.text: Ah~ This is a pot! A home for plants.

texts.speaker: Pwie
texts.text: Can I eat it?

texts.speaker: Hong Lu
texts.text: If you're talking about the pot, then... no, they're generally inedible.

texts.speaker: Don Quixote
texts.text: If thou speakest of the plant, then indeed! They are generally edible!

texts.speaker: Pwie
texts.text: Do they taste good?

texts.speaker: Hong Lu
texts.text: Hmm... That would depend on the plant.
Hearing that, Pwie plucked a leaf off the plant...
... and swallowed it.

texts.speaker: Don Quixote
texts.text: H-how does it taste, young Pwie?

texts.speaker: Pwie
texts.text: ... Bit bitter.

texts.speaker: Don Quixote
texts.text: Hm... Then allow me but the lightest dab of the tongue...

texts.speaker: Don Quixote
texts.text: ... Oho! 'Tis quite fragrant!

texts.speaker: Don Quixote
texts.text: *gag*
... Don Quixote continued to gag and retch for a while.

markers.notes: Attempting to cross the barrier before it unlocks.

texts.text: According to Meursault, this object has been assigned the symbolic function of denying passage. So, we can't cross it.
Wait, then...

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: not a barrier. It's just two rods connected with a rope, which means I can leap over this. It's safe to leap over this. We are not bound by these rules anyway...>

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <RAAAAAAAH!>

texts.speaker: Rodion
texts.text: Wh-huh? Dante, ya okay?

texts.speaker: Ishmael
texts.text: Did you trip trying to jump over that rope barrier?

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <I-I thought I could leap over it if I defined it as something else...>

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: ... Surface level self-deception cannot truly redefine a symbolic element, Manager.

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: Symbols are things nailed solidly into the deepest parts of consciousness. One must commit to a significant time investment should they wish to redefine the symbol... or be born with the "aptitude" to do so.

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <Ugh... Okay, then what about you? Can't you do what you did back at the escalator room?>

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: ... That was... mm.

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: That was made possible due to the particulars of that situation, in which I and a Giant were both gazing at the same symbol.

texts.speaker: Rodion
texts.text: What are ya two having so much fun gossipin' about?

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <Ah, just discussing ways to get around this thing. Turns out there isn't—let's just take the roundabout route.>

texts.speaker: Yi Sang
texts.text: This place is quiet to an uncanny degree. A "room of rest"... Truly, a chamber wherein one may rest freely.
Faust is staring into the empty space.

texts.speaker: Ishmael
texts.text: Ready when you are.

texts.speaker: Gregor
texts.text: If this is how it's gonna be... Well, I'll need a smoke.
I turn my head and see Ryōshū with a cigarette already pinched between her teeth, a wisp of smoke rising from the tip.
Hong Lu seems to be listening to whatever story Don Quixote's telling with genuine delight.
Sinclair is bombarding the blue lady with all kind of questions.
I don't think the conversation is going particularly well.
Don Quixote is recounting the acts and miracles of Fixers animatedly, in an effort to keep everyone's mood alight.
... Hong Lu seems to be the only one paying attention.
Heathcliff keeps circling the same spot restlessly.

texts.speaker: Outis
texts.text: It is rather frustrating that I am unable to be of assistance, trapped in this location. Should you need me, Executive Manager, I, Outis, am ready to be of service at your command.

texts.speaker: Rodion
texts.text: I'll be restin' here for a bit. Gimme a shout when it's time to leave~
Ryōshū has her eyes closed. The sizzle and hiss from the tip of the cigarette, however, tells me that she's not asleep.

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: I am ready, Manager.

parts.notes: Meursault (While Pwie is in the cocoon)

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: ... Pwie is alone.

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: We must return to the restaurant as quickly as our feet would take us, Manager.
They are standing by the entrance and refusing to budge, away from everyone else. Probably just anxious because of how crowded the restroom is.

texts.speaker: Pwie
texts.text: Do we... head out now?

texts.speaker: Eye-shopping Customer
texts.text: This trend had better die soon. I don't have a single patch of bare skin left for another polka dot.

markers.notes: Interact with Dubois' corpse after killing him

texts.text: Dubois lies dead.

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: Your instruction has been carried out, Manager.

texts.speaker: Ishmael
texts.text: ... I'll be honest. Killing someone who's been nothing but nice to us doesn't sit right with me.

texts.speaker: Rodion
texts.text: ... We need money if we're going upstairs.

texts.speaker: Rodion
texts.text: This was one way to get it... Unless we plan on squatting here selling clothes—or spending the whole day rummaging through corpses like the people outside.

texts.speaker: Ishmael
texts.text: Well, I'm not trying to guilt Dante for making that decision. They must've had something in mind when they ordered Meursault to do that.

texts.speaker: Ishmael
texts.text: What's all that?

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: Clothes that have fallen out of fashion due to the passing of the trend seasons.

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: Mm...

texts.speaker: Ishmael
texts.text: They're tucked away in such an out-of-the-way corner. It almost seems like someone was trying to h— Wh-what are you doing?

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: Rummaging through the pile for its contents.

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <... Are there anything of note other than eyeballs?>

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: Few scraps of leather with something written on them.

texts.speaker: Ishmael
texts.text: What do they say?

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: ... "The era of fluorescent plaid trend will be upon us soon, I know it."

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: "When that time comes, I'll take these clothes and rise to the runway, and—"

texts.speaker: Rodion
texts.text: ... I think that's enough, Meur. Let's move on.

texts.speaker: Ishmael
texts.text: Let's, uh... put those back into the pile.

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <... Let's do that.>
Mannequins stand on display.

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <... Meursault, can you get those things to look away?>

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: Yes, Manager.
Meursault punched the Mannequin in the face, rotating its head toward the wall. He repeated that process several more times against the other ones.

texts.speaker: Ishmael
texts.text: And we're suddenly letting off steam against random Mannequins because...?

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <Don't worry about it.>
A department-store directory. Damage has obscured much of it, but this department store definitely goes higher than the fourth floor.

texts.speaker: Rodion
texts.text: ... Hey, what's up with this map? Looks a bit weird to me...

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <Since the space we're inhabiting is more of a mental construct than a physical one, I wouldn't be surprised if its size is many times greater than its appearance might suggest.>

texts.speaker: Rodion
texts.text: Makes sense, this place is supposed to hold... 300 million people, after all.

texts.speaker: Rodion
texts.text: Oh, does it say which floor has the Golden Bough?

texts.speaker: Ishmael
texts.text: Why would anyone put that in the direc—Hm. I suppose that's not so implausible in here, lemme take a closer look.

texts.speaker: Rodion
texts.text: Darn. I don't see it.
Maybe I really was a tree in a past life.
When I encountered the diagram and structure of the mind in arboreal form...
... I felt drawn toward it and concluded it to be the rendering of the soul.
But I wonder... does the soul really take the shape of a tree?
Perhaps a tree is merely one way of representing it. The mind may be too unstable to possess a fixed structure at all.
Yet, the human forms I saw the Wings shape throughout the City converge again and again upon the structure of a tree.
The blueprint for N Corp.'s Sisyphe System alone suggests as much, does it not?

markers.notes: Returning to the Fount before finding Meursault.

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <Well, we returned here just in case, but...>

texts.speaker: Outis
texts.text: Executive Manager. Are you able to see Meursault's present surroundings? I recall you awakened a highly convenient ability in an effort to assist the more lacking members of our team.

texts.speaker: Outis
texts.text: Would you use that ability and tell us what you see?

texts.speaker: Gregor
texts.text: Yeah, Manager Bud. Tell us what you see.

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <I see a carpeted floor, and rows of clothes on display. Meursault's standing absolutely still.>

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <He's not tied up, and there's someone who looks like a store clerk beside him.>

texts.speaker: Outis
texts.text: Tch. Not much time has passed since the execution, and he already allows himself to be taken captive. An uncharacteristic display of incompetence coming from him—and on multiple fronts.

texts.speaker: Gregor
texts.text: Huh... Carpet, and clothes on display... Well, it's more than we had to go on before, at least.
Thankfully, Meursault is at the same spot he was last time. Well, no reason to dally...

markers.notes: Enter the Fount after bringing Pwie to F4.

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <Phew, looks like Pwie's able to come in here with the rest of us.>

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <... Is it just me, or do they seem somewhat less... hyper?>
Pwie's childlike curiosity seems to have been dampened and replaced with mild anxiety ever since entering the Fount.
Hmm... Must be because it's too crowded in here.

markers.notes: Corpse Pile after obtaining the Golden Hide.

texts.text: Something drenched in blood and tangled in sinews falls from the area we tore off the Golden Hide from.

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <Meursault, can you check what just fell?>

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: ... It appears to be a notebook, or a notepad of sorts.

texts.speaker: Rodion
texts.text: Hey... maybe it's a diary? Why don't we take a little peek?

texts.speaker: Ishmael
texts.text: I don't know, it feels a bit... icky peering into someone's diary.
Blood is slowly starting to soak the notebook and its contents... What should we do?
Most pages are soaked in blood and difficult to tell what it says.

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: I will read out loud what is legible.

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: "Godda— —otherfu— —tch—like it's some great undertaking to —ing on the —unway..."

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: "Cockly little— —eenhorn, know your place if you've just climbed up he—"
Meursault flipped past a few pages that have soaked up far too much blood to be legible.

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: "Abhorre— —tle shit. I knew it. I knew a— —like them couldn't have made it thi— —ar on their own.

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: "—thetic leech, working with Le— to— suck up all the— —of the— —artment store."

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: "I'm goi— to embarrass the— —hit out of them in— —of everyone."

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <... This department store's like this through all the floors no matter how high you climb, huh?>
There was something written in here, but it's gone now. The journal has soaked up too much blood.
Once, a child descended from a star and rained down as water.
Water that gives the mind material form. Cogito.
The experiments conducted using Cogito gave me the certainty:
The tree bears ten fruits.
The tree is divided into three domains.
And the order in which the tree is ascended carries significance.

texts.speaker: Heathcliff
texts.text: ... I ain't seein' what's so "luxury" about this place. Sure, it's a bit shiny, but it ain't that posh.
These items seem to have a more obvious golden glow to them than the items on the other floors. Even the ones that aren't glowing are meticulously decorated, obviously crafted with great care.

texts.speaker: Faust
texts.text: ... The items here appear to cost significantly more eyeballs than those available on other floors.

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: Carrying sufficient eyeballs is not enough. The Prestige Tier of the prospective client is also strictly screened before they are permitted to purchase these items.

texts.speaker: Heathcliff
texts.text: Oi, Clock.

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <Yeah?>

texts.speaker: Heathcliff
texts.text: ... Nah. I, hm. I've a bad feelin' about it.

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <What? Bad feeling about what?>

texts.speaker: Heathcliff
texts.text: Well... seein' as we're here anyway, I'm thinkin'—why don't we just take these and sell 'em on other floors? It ain't like there's anyone watchin' us...

texts.speaker: Faust
texts.text: That is—

texts.speaker: Heathcliff
texts.text: I get it, I get it! I was just floatin' the idea, nothin' more. Don't need another shite like that hair coupon incident happenin' again.
But I was just about to tell him that was a really good idea...

Ah, well. The display cases seem to be made from pretty durable material anyway.
We decided to move on.

markers.notes: Obtainable by killing the 3F Floor Manager during the Overseer's quest.
Obtained when bringing Pwie to L'Inamovible.
Obtained when interacting with L'Inamovible's corpse after bringing her Pwie.
Obtained after defeating Flannel and Felt.

texts.speaker: Skinhide Couch
texts.text: The fuck're you lookin' at! Get lost, fuckwit!

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <... I see. This couch came from the Furniture Hall.>

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <At least this room is well-lit.>

[Differential of Falling Series 1: "Cynthia"
This installation depicts the fall of Cynthia, the first Mannequin to fall in the Grand Magasin. The only large-scale installation in the series, it sets itself apart from the rest of the series by being the only piece to depict the precise moment her fall began in painstaking detail.]

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <Huh, now that I'm looking at it... this place has "installations," that aren't necessarily products.>

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <Do you think the Ring... has any presence here?>

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: Not all artistic endeavors are associated with the Ring's activities.

texts.speaker: Sinclair
texts.text: Still, these remind me of the things we saw back at the Ring Nursefather's gallery.

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <Maybe there's a note explaining what all this means. Assuming that the note survived...>

texts.speaker: Outis
texts.text: There indeed seem to be other "Differential of Falling" series in this area...

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <Well, they went out of their way to call it "Series 1," so it seems reasonable to assume that there's a "Series 2." Let's keep an eye out for it in case they have anything that might come in handy.>
It's a cash register. Reaching into its drawer to see if there's anything left... yields some eyeballs that were rolling around in its corner.

texts.speaker: Outis
texts.text: Not a bad get, Executive Manager. Take it—it should do us good to find and keep as many of these as we can.

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <Hm... Sure.>

texts.speaker: Sinclair
texts.text: W-wait, isn't this just straight-up thievery?

texts.speaker: Outis
texts.text: A more accurate designation for this strategy would be "field requisition tactics."
<color=#ebcaa2>I don't know, this strategy probably falls under the designation we call "larceny" here.</color>

texts.speaker: Outis
texts.text: ... *cough*

texts.speaker: Sinclair
texts.text: <Wait, we're not allowed to take eyeballs from cash registers? What about all those Mannequins we kill—I mean, "helped to the exit"?>
<color=#ebcaa2>Fuhu, you mean "criminal damage to property"?</color>

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <It doesn't matter inside this department store anyway, Sinclair. Take those eyeballs, Meursault.>
<color=#ebcaa2>Hah. You're no fun at all.</color>
<color=#ebcaa2>Just decided to ignore me now 'cuz you can't understand how jokes work, huh?</color>
Took the eyeballs.
Don't need these that badly.
There isn't anything left.

texts.speaker: Sinclair
texts.text: Huh, wonder what this is? Some kind of broadcast device?

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <It's a communication switchboard.>

texts.speaker: Sinclair
texts.text: What's a communication switchboard?

texts.speaker: Outis
texts.text: ... Have you had access to one of these devices in the past, Executive Manager?

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <Uh... No, I just read about it in a pamphlet once.>

texts.speaker: Outis
texts.text: ... As expected of our Executive Manager! Your rising passion for learning is most admirable indeed.
Outis seems to consider something for a moment.
Even if the mind does not take the form of a tree,
this method is worth attempting if the mind can be fixed into an arboreal model and interpreted through it.
Is language not the same?
We take mere sonic vibrations, devoid of meaning, and confine them within the form of language—and through it, we communicate.
I define this invisible, unstable mind as a tree.

texts.speaker: Sinclair
texts.text: Huh, these clothes are more expensive than the others.

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: That is because the display you are looking at is for this season's Prêt-à-porter items.

texts.speaker: Sinclair
texts.text: Prêt-à-por...ter?

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: Prêt-à-porter. It refers to made-to-stock, ready-to-wear items; those of higher quality and prestige, in particular.

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <These don't look so expensive anymore...>
[Prêt-à-porter. Contains 150% of the Golden Yarn compared to the Last Season's!]
Upon closer inspection, I notice that it contains only 0.00015% of the so-called "Golden Yarn." Doesn't seem anywhere near significant enough to warrant putting that on the advertisement.

texts.speaker: Sinclair
texts.text: Doesn't this mean that the last season's products had only 0.0001% Golden Yarn...?

texts.speaker: Outis
texts.text: ... I'm willing to bet that Whale chips from U Corp. have more Whale in them than this has Golden Yarn.
[Origami CollectioN ° 92, 2 of 5.]

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <I think we saw the "1 of 5" of the series on the first floor.>

texts.speaker: Sinclair
texts.text: Oh, right...! I remember learning about how some prints and sculptures are made with creating multiple identical copies in mind, only giving a different number to each "iteration" to distinguish them.

texts.speaker: Sinclair
texts.text: And even though each piece is pretty much indistinguishable from one another, their value might vary depending on the number they're given.

texts.speaker: Sinclair
texts.text: Then... the one on the first floor must be the first copy.

texts.speaker: Outis
texts.text: Most unremarkable rabble would've walked past it without a second thought... What impeccable perception you have! I expected no less of our Executive Manager!
<color=#ebcaa2>... Still a busy bee, huh?</color>
<color=#ebcaa2>Pff... Do you really have to try so hard for loose change? Aren't you rich enough to ignore a handful of eyeballs?</color>

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <... I can always afford to be richer, can't I?>

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: The manager replies that they can always afford to be richer.
Took some eyeballs lodged deep inside.

markers.notes: Interact with Arc Floor Lamp after killing him.
Interacting with the couch spawns Drawer enemies.
Obtained when inspecting the Happy Closet's remains.
Obtained during the Furniture Hall Quests.

texts.speaker: Pwie
texts.text: What's this?

texts.speaker: Hong Lu
texts.text: Ah~ This is a pot! A home for plants.

texts.speaker: Pwie
texts.text: Can I eat it?

texts.speaker: Hong Lu
texts.text: If you're talking about the pot, then... no, they're generally inedible.

texts.speaker: Don Quixote
texts.text: If thou speakest of the plant, then indeed! They are generally edible!

texts.speaker: Pwie
texts.text: Do they taste good?

texts.speaker: Hong Lu
texts.text: Hmm... That would depend on the plant.
Hearing that, Pwie plucked a leaf off the plant...
... and swallowed it.

texts.speaker: Don Quixote
texts.text: H-how does it taste, young Pwie?

texts.speaker: Pwie
texts.text: ... Bit bitter.

texts.speaker: Don Quixote
texts.text: Hm... Then allow me but the lightest dab of the tongue...

texts.speaker: Don Quixote
texts.text: ... Oho! 'Tis quite fragrant!

texts.speaker: Don Quixote
texts.text: *gag*
... Don Quixote continued to gag and retch for a while.
Of the two lamps, the lit one whispers something. Its lampshade silently swings like a pendulum.
Blink.
Blink.
Bliiiiink.
The lamp seems to blink gratefully.
BlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlink
... Not grateful, got it.
If you were born again, who or what would you want to become?
I think... I'd still want to be someone with a beautiful voice.
So that everyone would pay more attention to what I say.
Humanity originated from water, and water circulates within the human body. Perhaps this is why...
The star I wished for has already been irreversibly fixed into the form of water.
So long as I continue to think, Cogito will materialize what I desire.
That means if I can stay alive... if the Cogito I create can be made to function as the stars do...
Then there is still a way. A way to heal everyone.
This work is worth it. Perhaps that is why you never asked me to explain myself.
Isn't that right, Ayin...?
I leave it here—"Project Seed of Light Draft". The only way.
You should be capable of enduring it.
Which is why... I entrust this to you.

To my beloved junior,
- Carmen.

texts.speaker: Don Quixote
texts.text: Ah, young Pwie! Dost thy preference lean toward shoes on this side?

texts.speaker: Pwie
texts.text: I like 'em more than the ones on the other side.

texts.speaker: Pwie
texts.text: But I don't like like these...

texts.speaker: Don Quixote
texts.text: 'Tis fair to harbor such doubt, young Pwie! The journey for the perfect pair of shoes is most arduous indeed!

texts.speaker: Don Quixote
texts.text: Aha! Dost thou enjoy this pair of shoes, perchance? Behold the sharp angle of the toe cap, and the pullable band hither to prevent most unfortunate accidents when its strings are undone!

texts.speaker: Pwie
texts.text: ... I dunno.

texts.speaker: Don Quixote
texts.text: Very well! Then allow me to introduce these—
Don Quixote continued to showcase various shoes for Pwie, but none of those seemed to interest them much.
Pwie rested their hand on a couch.

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <...! Meursault! Grab Pwie!>

texts.speaker: Pwie
texts.text: Wh-what...?

texts.speaker: Pwie
texts.text: Did I do something... wrong?

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: You did not. But... laying your hands on random objects in here could cause... problems.

texts.speaker: Don Quixote
texts.text: Verily! For doing so may anger its owner!

texts.speaker: Pwie
texts.text: It has an owner...? I didn't know. Nobody bought it, so... I thought it didn't have one.

texts.speaker: Don Quixote
texts.text: ‘Tis… true. Yet…
Pwie barraged us with questions.

texts.speaker: Hong Lu
texts.text: Ah, a slide~! A place for children, maybe?

texts.speaker: Pwie
texts.text: What's a slide?

texts.speaker: Hong Lu
texts.text: It's a playground ride. You climb the ladders on one side, and sliiiide down the decline on the other side.

texts.speaker: Hong Lu
texts.text: Would you like to give it a try, Pwie?

texts.speaker: Pwie
texts.text: I don't like going down...

texts.speaker: Hong Lu
texts.text: It's more fun than you might think~

texts.speaker: Don Quixote
texts.text: Indeed, Pwie! Not once have I met a child who disliketh the slide. Prithee, give it a slide!

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <We don't have much time, guys... How about we come back to it later?>

texts.speaker: Don Quixote
texts.text: Prithee, Manager Esquire! It will only take but a moment!

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <... Fine. It's just a slide, after all.>

texts.speaker: Don Quixote
texts.text: Now, young Pwie... climb from this side, and—ah, be sure to stretch both of thy legs forward! And allow the declining path to carry thee...

texts.speaker: Don Quixote
texts.text: ... as I have demonstrated!!

texts.speaker: Pwie
texts.text: Climb... from this side, and...

texts.speaker: Pwie
texts.text: ... That was fun.

texts.speaker: Hong Lu
texts.text: Watching you have fun makes me happy, too~

texts.speaker: Pwie
texts.text: ... Can I go again?

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <... Why not.>

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: The manager has given their authorization. You may go again.

texts.speaker: Pwie
texts.text: Woo.
Pwie happily bounced up the stairs to the top of the slide once again.

texts.speaker: Pwie
texts.text: I wanna go again. I wanna go again.

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: ... Manager.

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <... We should probably get going.>

texts.speaker: Don Quixote
texts.text: 'Tis not to disagree with thee, Manager Esquire... Yet hast thou not seen how much joy this activity granteth the child? Just once more, and we shall carry on with haste.

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <... Sure.>
Pwie happily bounced up the stairs to the top of the slide once again.
... Pwie runs to the top of the slide again without even asking us.

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <... Uh... Guys, we really gotta...>

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: You can ride it some more later.

texts.speaker: Pwie
texts.text: Later...? When?
In the end, we let Pwie play as much as they wanted.
... Is it really that fun?

texts.speaker: Pwie
texts.text: Did you... want to go on the slide too, Dante?

texts.speaker: Hong Lu
texts.text: Are you thinking of riding the slide right now, Manager?
It's not much fun.
It's a slide. Is the fun part going down... or climbing back up after?
Found a piece of paper inside the drawer.
[MISSING PERSON]
[Description: Burn scar on the face, scarf, leather bag...]
[Last Seen: Plaza Sisyphe, 1F, ■■■ Memorial Hall]

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <... Burn scar?>

texts.speaker: Hong Lu
texts.text: Someone you know?

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <... Maybe. Where's Plaza Sisyphe, though?>
Meursault said nothing. He stared at the paper for a moment, seemingly lost in thought, then shook his head as if to say he didn't know.
[Chevalier : A objet containing the total history of Le Noir Handbags Hall, which has spearheaded the art of handbag design since the Grand Magasin Sisyphe's inception.]

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <... Hey, this one looks artsy.>

texts.speaker: Don Quixote
texts.text: Ooooh! Though it paleth before dearest Rocinante, 'tis an excellent steed indeed!

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <... I think the horse just glared at you?>

texts.speaker: Don Quixote
texts.text: P-prithee, accept mine apologies, young steed of... wood. Forgive my... comment most foolish.
It does not reply.
If you were born again, who or what would you want to become?
I think... I'd still want to be someone with a beautiful voice.
So that everyone would pay more attention to what I say.
Humanity originated from water, and water circulates within the human body. Perhaps this is why...
The star I wished for has already been irreversibly fixed into the form of water.
So long as I continue to think, Cogito will materialize what I desire.
That means if I can stay alive... if the Cogito I create can be made to function as the stars do...
Then there is still a way. A way to heal everyone.
This work is worth it. Perhaps that is why you never asked me to explain myself.
Isn't that right, Ayin...?
I leave it here—"Project Seed of Light Draft". The only way.
You should be capable of enduring it.
Which is why... I entrust this to you.

To my beloved junior,
- Carmen.
Light cascades in through the tall window.
After fixing it in my gaze for a while, the patterns begin to dance and ripple.

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <... This is...?>
Things that should not be visible begin to unveil themselves.
Light cascades in through the tall window.

Schools of fish are swimming gently through the water beyond the glass window.
A large crowd is walking between the glass walls, exploring the aquatic life.

markers.notes: Corridor Windows (after obtaining the Golden Shroud)

texts.text: Light cascades in through the tall window.
There is a large plaza, so vast that its edges can barely be fathomed. At the center of the plaza stands a tall building, and at its base people come and go in busy strides.
Light cascades in through the tall window.

Faint ray of light shimmers through the gloom of the stiflingly narrow tunnel. There are mounds of cans sitting along the walls, constricting the already cramped hallway.
People are crawling through the passage that is more like a cavernous crawl space.
Light cascades in through the tall window.
People are shouting and hollering at each other. It is hard to make out what it is they are yelling about, but... the sight is reminiscent of a trial.

markers.notes: Obtained by trading the 'Bone' to or killing Sous Chef during the Overseer's quest.
Obtained when interacting with the larva in the Shore.

texts.speaker: Le Rouge Porter
texts.text: Should've brought another pair of hands...

texts.speaker: Le Rouge Porter
texts.text: Who the hell are you people?

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <Are you waiting for something here?>

texts.speaker: Faust
texts.text: We are curious as to what you are awaiting here.

texts.speaker: Le Rouge Porter
texts.text: Need to strip the Hides from B3 and haul 'em back. Don't know why, but supplies haven't been coming through lately—

texts.speaker: Le Rouge Porter
texts.text: ...! Wait. Shh... I can hear the Voice again!
The Rouge porter shoved past us, pressed themself against the wall, and broke into a blissful grin.
The door is blocked. Pressing an ear against it reveals a jumble of noises beyond—voices, footsteps, and more.

texts.speaker: Pwie
texts.text: What are they all doing in there? All huddled in a group...

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <Huddled in a group...? Who?>

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: The Manager asks whether you can see through the blocked door.

texts.speaker: Pwie
texts.text: Blocked door...? It's not blocked, though...

texts.speaker: Faust
texts.text: It is likely that we and Pwie are looking at different things.
Pwie hovered in front of the door for a while, then their curiosity seemingly sated—or simply dwindled—turned around and began looking elsewhere.

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: Mm.

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <This one won't be opening, it seems.>

texts.speaker: Pwie
texts.text: What happened?

texts.speaker: Faust
texts.text: We were refused entry.

texts.speaker: Pwie
texts.text: We can't... go in?

texts.speaker: Faust
texts.text: No. It appears that Meursault does not meet the conditions required to enter.

texts.speaker: Pwie
texts.text: Just like me.
Pwie smiled lightly, then stood a step closer to Meursault.

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <Meursault!>

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <Are you all right?!>

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: I've sustained dermal lacerations, but they are not severe enough to impede me.
As Meursault rises and briskly dusts himself off, I could hear someone—or something—snickering at him.
Knocked on the door, but there's no response. Or any signs of life, for that matter.
There is nothing but the chilling silence.

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <I think we're being avoided...>
It looks as though a thick blackout curtain has been drawn behind the narrow window.
... Every so often, something makes a wet squelch as though something is being wrung out.
Leaned in toward the curtain again to listen some more.
A wet patter sounded from within. A moment later, the curtain gave a small twitch with a sharp smack.
... Something appears to have sprayed out and splattered all over it.
No other sounds follow.
... Though every so often, I think I hear droplets falling from beneath the curtain.
The door opens onto an empty space drowned in darkness.
Last time, entering this door led us to the Fount.

texts.speaker: Pwie
texts.text: ... So dark. Don't go in there.

texts.speaker: Gregor
texts.text: 100% agreed.

texts.speaker: Gregor
texts.text: Uh... We're not going in there, are we, Manager Bud?
Considering what happened when we tried this entrance before the Liquidation... it would be common sense not to try it again.
But the Grand Magasin this time has changed in some significant ways since our last visit.
Therapy or conversation cannot heal the soul.
Measured against this schema, psychotherapy is no more than a primitive stopgap.
But now that I know the shape of the human mind, could I not diagnose and heal it?
If so, it may be possible to heal not only N Corp., where I was born, but also the terrible suffering that has enveloped the City itself.
It may be possible to heal the people of the City who are afflicted by an illness that makes them unable to know who they are in their journey toward death.

texts.speaker: Boucher
texts.text: ... I make these benches, and no one sits on 'em anyway.

texts.speaker: Boucher
texts.text: Except for Head Chef—no, what she's doing doesn't even count as cooking.

texts.speaker: Boucher
texts.text: I'd much rather smash this whole business to pieces. Yeah, that's much sweeter to my ears.
He's muttering to himself as he slams the cleaver down on chunk after chunk of meat. ... Probably not the best time to chat him up.
There's a ticket laid atop the drawing of a ladder.
[A ticket alone cannot take you anywhere.]
[It is mererly a promise to bring you somewhere.]
[Thus, those who know their destinations nail the ladder down as a ticket.]

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <Who do you suppose left this here?>

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: Perhaps a stranger struggling to make use of the escalator all... no, that doesn't seem very probable. This is most likely nothing more than Giant mischief.

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <You mean people like Jeanne... or the Chaplain... left this here?>

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: ... Or Mother. Or one of the current Giants' predecessors, perhaps.
There's a compass laid atop the drawing of a ladder.
[I'm quite fond of compasses. It abides by the absolute rule of cardinal directions—north, east, south, and west... Beautiful.]
[One may harbor certain doubts in their hearts, yes: are these rules the "right" rules? Does the compass work according to the rules? ... Indeed, all valid concerns.]
[But the point of a compass is to guide you when you're lost. You get the idea.]
[All good? Very well. I'll be clocking out now.]

texts.speaker: Pwie
texts.text: What's "clocking out"?

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: It means to wrap up a day's work and return home.

texts.speaker: Pwie
texts.text: ... You have to leave home to work?

texts.speaker: Gregor
texts.text: Well... some works can be done from home. But for most people, "work" means leaving home.

texts.speaker: Pwie
texts.text: Then... I think work kinda sucks.

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <... Is it just me, or did that sound just like what Bamboo-hatted Kim would say?>

texts.speaker: Pwie
texts.text: Everybody wants to go home, but they still gotta hold that in and leave home...
As Meursault continued to answer Pwie's stream of questions about "home," Faust quietly approached me from the side.

texts.speaker: Faust
texts.text: ... There is something about "going home." Though the note may have been written from a Giant's point of view... it may also imply that there is, in fact, a way out of here.

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <... Sure hope so. This time, we'll succeed.>
Through the window, a huge, unidentifiable thing is feeding what looks like hide into a hole in the wall.

texts.speaker: Pwie
texts.text: I wanna see, too.
Pwie stands on tiptoes, trying to see what's beyond the window.

texts.speaker: Faust
texts.text: That aperture is the kind commonly employed for waste disposal in multi-unit residences. It is also referred to as "dust chute."

texts.speaker: Gregor
texts.text: But... isn't this just a detached house?

texts.speaker: Faust
texts.text: That is common sense as established within the City, Herr Gregor. It is difficult to apply the same standard to the way things are in the Symbolic.

texts.speaker: Gregor
texts.text: Huh... you're saying a dust chute isn't a common-sense concept here then...?
... Once again, I pull the two Sinners apart before their squabbling can get worse.

markers.notes: Fish Market Tank (Top row, 2nd from the right)

texts.speaker: Pwie
texts.text: ... It looks like it's hurting.
Pwie pointed to the bottom of the water tank.
Something shriveled and dried up is slowly getting flattened beneath the weight pressing down on it.

texts.speaker: Gregor
texts.text: Oof... yeah, that's kinda rough to look at. Want me to pull it out?

texts.speaker: Pwie
texts.text: But... then the ones on top would get hurt...

texts.speaker: Gregor
texts.text: Fair point... Then should we pull all of them out? Not sure that's such a good idea, though...

texts.speaker: Faust
texts.text: ... It's too late.
Just as Faust said, it was already too late. The thing being flattened gave one last sickening whimper before it was crushed completely.

texts.speaker: Pwie
texts.text: ...If you die, it doesn't hurt anymore. But... I still don't like it.

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: Because death is the end.

texts.speaker: Pwie
texts.text: ... Death is the end? But... Even if they die, they can start again.

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: That distinction is meaningless. The new existence is not a continuation of the previous one.
Pwie turned toward another being that existed within the water tank and observed it thoughtfully, watching as it was slowly crushed to death under the weight of others.
Pwie's eyes dart around.
Pwie is poking a creature wriggling around inside the water tank. It seems to have drawn their interest.
Gheee...
Poke, poke, poke... Did they just poke it in the eye?
GHEEEEEEEHHHHH!

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <... Meursault, can you stop Pwie from doing that?>
Meursault picked Pwie up and put them down a good distance away from the water tank.

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <Huh, a creature inside a water tank... I wonder if it's food?>

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: .. Yes. It appears to be one of the cooking ingredients sold at the Food Court.

texts.speaker: Gregor
texts.text: ... Darn, do we have to pay for this? Pwie just poked it, and y'know, with the "you touch it, you buy it" rule and everything...

texts.speaker: Faust
texts.text: According to the announcement heard upon our entry to the Grand Magasin, it is likely that this degree of contact is permitted.

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <Hey, wait a minute... Is this another larva? Looks a bit like that larva from Boucher's storehouse.>

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: It has been altered to fool the viewer. Patches of leather and flesh were sown together to resemble the outward appearance of a larva.

texts.speaker: Gregor
texts.text: Really? Who'd lie about this kinda stuff?
What blooms there is the rot. Is it even edible?

texts.speaker: Pwie
texts.text: Can I eat this?

texts.speaker: Gregor
texts.text: No way, kid.

texts.speaker: Pwie
texts.text: Why? Why not?

texts.speaker: Gregor
texts.text: Well, I mean... just look at it, it's spoiled. It'll give you the rumblies.

texts.speaker: Pwie
texts.text: ... We can't eat what's spoiled? Is rumblies... bad?

texts.speaker: Gregor
texts.text: Oh, uh... Well, that's...

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: ... You may eat it.
With Meursault's permission, Pwie takes a big bite out of the meat.

texts.speaker: Gregor
texts.text: H-hold on! I get this isn't the most normal place, Meursault, but you can't just tell that kid to eat a rotten piece of—

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: The "common sense" outside the department store does not apply here. That cut of meat is but another article of clothing here, and considering that Pwie is a product of the Grand Magasin... it is unlikely to cause any issues.

texts.speaker: Pwie
texts.text: I'm done. Don't wanna eat more.

texts.speaker: Gregor
texts.text: *sigh* Fine, guess you're right. There's no rule saying Pwie should eat the same things that we do, but...
For a moment, Gregor gave a conflicted look toward the spoiled piece of meat... then turned away.

markers.notes: Obtained by killing the King of Needleworks during the Overseer's quest.
Obtained by trading Scissors to Palette or killing Putty during the Overseer's quest.
Obtained when killing the B2F Floor Manager.

texts.text: The machine looks complicated to operate.

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <Meursault, do you know how to operate this?>

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: I am not familiar with the work procedures of Sisyphe's lower floors.
Meanwhile, Outis began manipulating the machine's complex display.

texts.speaker: Outis
texts.text: Hm... I do not yet understand the operating principle, but I have a general grasp of the structure.

texts.speaker: Outis
texts.text: The interface presents three functions: extraction, spinning, and dyeing. Your orders, Executive Manager?
Three buttons appear on the display Outis indicates.
With a disconcerting whir, the machine sucked a patch of Meursault's skin onto its surface.

texts.speaker: Ryōshū
texts.text: Huh. These threads are O. of a K.
With a disconcerting whir, the machine sucked a patch of Meursault's skin onto its surface.
With a disconcerting whir, the machine sucked a patch of Meursault's skin onto its surface.

texts.speaker: Outis
texts.text: ... Are... you going to press it again, Executive Manager?
With a disconcerting whir, the machine sucked a patch of Meursault's skin onto its surface.

texts.speaker: Ryōshū
texts.text: You want it S.I.T.?

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: She is asking whether your objective is to have the skin "split into threads," Manager.

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <N-no, that's not what I'm doing... But has Sinclair ever interpreted that one before?>

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: He has interpreted "S.E.N.I.T." before on the bus. It stands for "split every nerve into threads."

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <I really don't remember what the context was when she said it.>
A spool of thread plopped out of the contraption.
It appears to be thread made from... Meursault's skin.
There shouldn't be any reason to press this button again.
The threads twang lightly as the machine pulls them tight.
They're starting to multiply...

texts.speaker: Needlekin Laborer
texts.text: ... Uh, we weren't told anything about increased production volume.

texts.speaker: Needlekin Laborer 2
texts.text: Slowly-slow! Gently-gentle! You'll break it!
... The customers working nearby are glaring daggers at us.
... The accusatory glares around me are too sharp to risk pressing it again.
A warning states that no dye is available.
Nothing happened.

texts.speaker: Outis
texts.text: With all due respect, Executive Manager... may I ask what exactly it is that you intend to accomplish?

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <... I mean... Sometimes you just want to mash some buttons, right?>
As I try to hammer the button once more, something taps my elbow.
I turned to find Ryōshū's scabbard, Araya.
For a moment, I could swear I heard it say, "You really should stop acting like a kid..."
Yeah, I should stop. This is getting ridiculous.

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <I heard something like the rumble of a train last time coming from here...>
A sound resembling the rumble of a train comes from beyond the door. I move closer to investigate, but unlike before, I can't see any light.

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <I can hear the sound, but...>
Curious, Pwie approached me as I inspected the door...

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <Huh? Wait!>
... and disappeared into the crevice.

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: ... They will return soon, Manager.
Meursault was right. Pwie returned in less than a minute.

texts.speaker: Pwie
texts.text: Threads are running inside. And then they stopped, and then ran again. Why are they doing that?

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <... I wanna know, too.>

texts.speaker: Outis
texts.text: ... It seems this child can enter places we cannot, just like the other customers in the department store.

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <We'll need to pay special attention to our back and make sure they're following us.>

texts.speaker: Pwie
texts.text: My legs hurt. I wanna sit down.
Pwie points to a sofa splashed with all sorts of colors.

texts.speaker: Ryōshū
texts.text: If you want to sit, then you need only sit.
Ryōshū picked Pwie up and set them down on the sofa.
Putty quietly glared back and forth between the sofa and Ryōshū, then turned her attention to the dyes without a word.

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <So it was okay to sit here...? Then Iet me take a break too...>
As I move to sit down, Putty raises one of her awl-sharp legs.

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <... Yeah, never mind. I'll just stand.>

texts.speaker: Palette
texts.text: This sofa's nice and squishy, but it's not exactly sturdy. The kid's fine, but it'll probably cave right in if one of you sits on it.

texts.speaker: Outis
texts.text: Hm. Perhaps we should purchase a sofa for your exclusive use from the Furniture Hall on 4F, Executive Manager.

texts.speaker: Outis
texts.text: A sofa that follows you around, allowing you to sit whenever and wherever necessary so your legs do not tire...

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <... It's okay. I think I'm fine on my feet.>
The shape of this tree is but an outcome of compiling my eclectic discoveries; I did not prescribe this form.
Just as the human body has an anatomical diagram, this tree is a diagram of the human mind.
To treat the afflicted, one must first understand the body.
Yet no one has thus far completed a visualization of the human soul—or consciousness—let alone devised the means of systematizing its structure.
There's an abandoned numbered ticket.

texts.speaker: Pwie
texts.text: What's this?

texts.speaker: Ryōshū
texts.text: A numbered ticket. Something idiots take to secure a place in a queue.

texts.speaker: Pwie
texts.text: ... So why do they wait in line? Can't they just go in?

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text:
They can't, because everyone in line desires to be the first to enter.
Therefore, they collectively agree to create a rule called "first-come, first-served," and imbue resultant queue with legitimacy.

texts.speaker: Pwie
texts.text: Mm... I dunno. Do they have to? Just 'cuz everyone says so?

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: Yes. Because everyone in the queue shares the same faith that all worthy goals requires its pursuers to wait, and because they have faith that waiting is fair to all, they abide by it.

texts.speaker: Pwie
texts.text: Fair...

texts.speaker: Outis
texts.text: ... Fairness is an illusion. Though it might seem like they're all waiting in the same queue under the same rules, that's just not the way the world spins.
A container filled with red dye. "TO BE DELIVERED TO B3" is written along its side.

texts.speaker: Pwie
texts.text: I like this color.

texts.speaker: Ryōshū
texts.text: Oho?

texts.speaker: Ryōshū
texts.text: T.A.R.T.?

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <... Tart? What's dessert got to do with this?>

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: "Torrid and rhapsodic taste," Manager.

texts.speaker: Pwie
texts.text: I dunno. Seeing this color just makes me feel calm.

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <Hey, here's a bucket of transparent liquid. Maybe it's L'Incolore?>

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: ... We cannot say for certain, Manager. It may be a different fluid that is just as transparent.

texts.speaker: Pwie
texts.text: Transparent dye...?

texts.speaker: Pwie
texts.text: No, no. This isn't transparent.

texts.speaker: Ryōshū
texts.text: Oho, it's not? Then what does it look like to you?

texts.speaker: Pwie
texts.text: It's... quiet... sad... and splish-splashy.

texts.speaker: Outis
texts.text: Not the most appropriate collection of adjectives for describing color, are they?

texts.speaker: Ryōshū
texts.text: Dilettante. Art isn't just a simple observation and recreation of visible colors.

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <Regardless, Pwie isn't exactly doing art right now, are they?>
Pwie stared into the bucket for a while, then turned away.

markers.notes: Obtained when giving all Golden Hide pieces to the Overseer.
Obtained when completing the cutting machine quest.

texts.text: No matter the manner of its inception, the moment something acquires material existence, it is without exception assigned a structure.
I concluded that this could be regarded as human fate.
This is not fate in the narrative sense. There is nothing metaphysical or grand about it—nothing more complicated than a genetic sequence.
The cells of a fish may differentiate into all kinds of forms, but ultimately, the fish cannot leave the water. Once a fish has abandoned its aquatic existence, it is no longer categorized as "fish."
Such a structure is also observed in human beings. An equivalent fate.
And by some stroke of coincidence, that structure took the shape of a tree.
The tree's name is Sephirot.
Voices can be heard among the passing shadows.

texts.speaker: Impatient Customer
texts.text: How far are you gonna go over one lousy hide?

texts.speaker: Impatient Customer
texts.text: The season's gonna change soon and we're due to move up anyway... can't we just bring any old leather?

texts.speaker: Adamant Customer
texts.text: Nope. Definitely not.

texts.speaker: Adamant Customer
texts.text: The more you break leather in... the more it molds itself to you.

texts.speaker: Adamant Customer
texts.text: The color, the creases, even the way it moves... it all starts to take after me!

texts.speaker: Adamant Customer
texts.text: Those leathers over there... they haven't been broken in to me.
Human leather that's been laid out to dry.

texts.speaker: Ishmael
texts.text: ... This is disgusting.

texts.speaker: Yi Sang
texts.text: It is as though they have unfolded the body, akin to the planar figure of a polyhedron, only human...

texts.speaker: Yi Sang
texts.text: This is a sight most inapt for the eyes of children.
Yi Sang carefully moved to the side, blocking Pwie from looking at the piece of leather.
Considering where we are, however... I don't think it'll do much good.

texts.speaker: Ishmael
texts.text: Ugh... That smell... It's even worse than Whale odor.

texts.speaker: Pwie
texts.text: *sniff* *sniff*

texts.speaker: Pwie
texts.text: Smells good.

texts.speaker: Ishmael
texts.text: ... Really? This smell?

texts.speaker: Pwie
texts.text: Mhm. Smells savory and rich.

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: It is not so out of the ordinary for them to perceive it as such.

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: Food dehydration is a process by which the ingredient's unique flavors may be more vividly conveyed.

texts.speaker: Pwie
texts.text: Does it smell tasty to you too, Meursault?

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: Had this been jerky rather than leather... I imagine it would have smelled good to me, too.

texts.speaker: Pwie
texts.text: What's the difference?
Meursault patiently answered Pwie's questions as they kept coming.
